# ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes - 2024

## Section 6: Glycemic Targets

### 6.1 Assessment of Glycemic Control

A1C testing is recommended for patients with diabetes:
- At least twice yearly for patients meeting treatment goals
- Quarterly for patients with changed therapy or not meeting goals

### 6.2 Glycemic Goals

HbA1c target should be <7% for most adults with diabetes who are not pregnant.

A more stringent HbA1c target (such as <6.5%) may be appropriate for:
- Selected patients with short duration of diabetes
- Type 2 diabetes treated with lifestyle or metformin only
- Long life expectancy
- No significant cardiovascular disease

A less stringent HbA1c target (such as <8%) may be appropriate for patients with:
- History of severe hypoglycemia
- Limited life expectancy
- Advanced microvascular or macrovascular complications
- Extensive comorbid conditions
- Long-standing diabetes

### 6.3 Hypoglycemia

Hypoglycemia is the major limiting factor in glycemic management.
It is recommended for patients at risk to have glucagon available.

## Section 9: Pharmacologic Approaches to Glycemic Treatment

### 9.1 Metformin

Metformin is the preferred initial pharmacologic agent for type 2 diabetes.

### 9.2 GLP-1 Receptor Agonists

GLP-1 receptor agonists are recommended for patients with:
- Established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease
- Indicators of high cardiovascular risk
- Heart failure
- Chronic kidney disease

These medications have demonstrated cardiovascular and renal benefits.
